figures.evidence: Re-derived. start() in link_host.c refuses a request while one is pending; LINK_HOST_TIMEOUT_MS is 1000 (link_host.h:29); LINK_MAX_REGS 32 (link_msg.h:21) and LINK_CAN_REGS_PER_FRAME 4 give LINK_CAN_MAX_FRAMES 8 (link_can.h:69-72). exchange() (main.c:1652-1719) sends every frame of one request, then waits until the answer or the request's own timeout. can_twai_send is called only at main.c:1663, selftest.c:33 and :66. A stalled IO board still acknowledges but cannot answer, so outside the self-test a stall under 1000 ms sees one request's frames: 8. In the self-test, probes wait for the 50 ms timeout (can_selftest.c:142, :209) and status requests retry on a 50 ms deadline (selftest.c:28-43); the only shorter gap is last probe to next status request, 20 ms receive plus 2 ms delay. 10 frames would need 8 x 50 + 22 = 422 ms > 400 ms, so 9. 3 ms: 8 (one write).
figures.source: checkout 10b0bade34de shared/link/link_host.c:32-60, shared/link/include/link_host.h:29, link_msg.h:21, link_can.h:69-72, firmware/panel/main/main.c:196, :1652-1719, firmware/panel/main/selftest.c:28-101, shared/can/can_selftest.c:142, :200-215

figures.evidence: Recounted: nominal before the switch SOF 1 + ID 11 + RRS + IDE + FDF + res = 16; counted at the data rate BRS, ESI, DLC 4, stuff count 4 (3 Gray-coded plus parity, CiA), CRC 17, 6 fixed stuff bits, CRC delimiter = 34; nominal after ACK, ACK delimiter, EOF 7, IFS 3 = 12. 28 us + 34 x 0.2 us = 34.8 us. 400,000/34.8 = 11,494.3, plus one = 11,495; 3,000/34.8 = 86.2, plus one = 87. Counting BRS and the delimiter wholly fast and leaving out dynamic stuff bits both shorten the frame, so the count is an upper bound. AN5348 Rev 6 Figure 2: EOF 7 bits, IFS 3 bits; line 1689: data phase ends at the sample point of the CRC delimiter. CiA: switch at the sample point of BRS. The CiA page also writes '8-bit stuff-bit counter'; a longer counter only lengthens the frame, so the bound holds. 29-bit: 19 bits more, 53.8 us, 7,435 and 56; classic 47 us, 8,511 and 64: recomputed equal.

figures.evidence: IOBoard.md:57 and :238 read 'the external CAN transceiver is in standby while the enable is low'; Research.md R2 row (:280) and V30 (:590) name the external CAN transceiver's standby among the gates. Monostable.md at 23c82ca line 30 names as gates only the buffer's output enable and the high-side switches on the servo rail and the ESC pack, and says nothing on CAN. No source found that states otherwise.

Monostable.md at 23c82ca: :111 enable node upper bound 185 ms, :113 'Power switch open after the enable node falls | 5 ms', :114 reserve 10 ms, :115 deadline 200 ms; 185 + 5 + 10 = 200. The page gives no row for a transceiver; the 5 ms power-switch budget applied to it fits the deadline. The buffer's own row (under 1 us) is a logic output-enable measured in test, not a budget line.

DroneCAN 4.4: 'DroneCAN operates on CANFD', 'frames can be up to 64 bytes in length'. 4.1 defines the classic transport. README.md:108-111 and STATUS.md:383 name DroneCAN; a grep of the tree's .md files finds no other CAN application protocol (CONTRIBUTING.md:22 and README-de.md:116 name it the same way).

DroneCAN section 8 table: 1000 kbit/s is the highest recommended bit rate. DroneCAN 4.4 Bus rates: 'nominal bit rate of 1MBps, with payload switching to 1, 2, 4, 5 or 8 MBit depending on hardware capabilities'. SLLSFJ3D page 1: 'to 5 megabits per second (Mbps). Up to 8Mbps operation in simpler networks is possible'.

CAN bus parameters table, 1000 kbit/s: valid sample point 75% to 90%, recommended 87.5%, max bus length 40 m, max stub 0.3 m. Text: 'based on the assumption that the propagation delay does not exceed 5 ns/m, not including additional delay times of CAN transceivers and other components'.
D-Sub pin 3 CAN Ground: 'Must be interconnected with Ground (pin 6) within the device'. Micro connector pin 4 Ground; M8 pin 5 Ground. The tree states no isolation for the port.

D-Sub and M8: 'Devices that deliver power to the bus are required to provide 23.0-30.0 V on the bus power line, 24 V nominal'; bus-powered devices expect 18.0 to 30.0 V. Micro: 5.0 to 5.5 V. A CAN line shorted to the bus power pin therefore sees up to 30.0 V.

Micro connector: 'Devices that deliver power to the bus are required to provide 5.0-5.5 V on the bus power line'. IOBoard.md:56 gives 5 V (F6) through the link cable and :177 says the cable carries the display's supply. V81 is open (Research.md:641). The value states that it is taken by analogy.

DS20001801K section 5.6: 'A maximum node-to-node oscillator variation of 1.7% is allowed'; half is ±0.85 %. Recomputed with DS20005282C Eq. 3-6 and 3-7 (per-node df, two nodes at opposite limits): IO board side 8 TQ, PHSEG2 2, SJW 2: 2/160 = 1.25 %, 2/(2 x 102) = 0.98 %; TWAI 20 TQ, tseg2 5, SJW 4: 4/400 = 1.0 %, 5/510 = 0.98 %. The MCP2518FD's 40 TQ timing at 75 % gives the same ratios. ±0.85 % is inside 0.98 %. Tried to refute: DS20005282C section 3.8.5, which the value cites, states 'A maximum node-to-node oscillator variation of 1.58% is allowed'; halved that is ±0.79 %, tighter than ±8,500 ppm. The conditions at the link's own timing, 0.98 % a node, are the governing bound, so ±8,500 ppm holds as a limit; the value's 'tighter of two sources' leaves the 1.58 % sentence out.

Mutter, iCC 2013, pages 08-21 to 08-23: condition 1 sjwA/(2 x 10 x btA), 2 min(ps1A,ps2A)/(2(13btA - ps2A)), 3 sjwD/(2 x 10 x btD), 4 min(ps1A,ps2A)/(2[(6btD - ps2D)BRPD/BRPA + 7btA]), 5 (sjwD - max(0, BRPA/BRPD - 1))/(2[(2btA - ps2A)BRPA/BRPD + ps2D + 4btD]). Recomputed at 40 MHz, BRP 1, btA 40, 90 % (ps2A 4), btD 8, 75 % (ps2D 2, sjwD 2): 0.50 %, 4/1032 = 0.3876 %, 1.25 %, 4/652 = 0.61 %, 2/220 = 0.91 %. Data sample point 87.5 %: condition 5 = 1/218 = 0.46 %. At 8 TQ a data bit only 75 % and 87.5 % exist. At the 87.5 % nominal point condition 2 = 5/1030 = 0.4854 %. Minimum 0.3876 % = ±3,876 ppm.
figures.source: https://www.can-cia.org/fileadmin/cia/documents/proceedings/2013_mutter.pdf (vendors.py fetch, HTTP 200); DroneCAN section 8 sample points; DS20006027B Table 7-3

The datasheet figures read correctly: Table 7-3 FOSC1,4M/20M/40M within ±0.5 % for a crystal or resonator (the external digital clock row, 2 to 40 MHz, carries no ±0.5 %), FDRIFT 10 ppm at 4 MHz, TOSCSTAB 3 ms. The comparison is wrong: 'The bus sets ±8,500 ppm on the link (V26), inside the ±0.5 % input limit'. ±8,500 ppm is 0.85 %, wider than ±0.5 % (±5,000 ppm), not inside it. On the link the part's own ±0.5 % input limit is the tighter and binding one, which is what the shortlist's requirement row says ('the round 2 crystal is held to ±5,000 ppm or tighter'). On the external port ±3,876 ppm (V27) is the tighter one, as stated.

Table 9-4: FOSC1,4M, 20M and 40M each nominal ±0.5 %; FDRIFT 10 ppm at 4 MHz; TOSCSTAB 3 ms from POR. A crystal meeting ±5,000 ppm on the link and ±3,876 ppm on the external port is inside the part's range.

figures.figure: re-rank drop: External CAN transceiver: TLE9252VSK (C540122)
figures.evidence: First reason does not hold. The requirement reads 'VCC from the 3.3 V logic rail or the 5 V rail' (IOBoard.md:337-338). TLE9252V's VCC, the transmitter supply, is 4.5 to 5.5 V (Table 3, P_8.2.2), from the 5 V rail. VBAT (5.5 to 40 V, P_8.2.1) is a second supply pin the requirement does not name. The board has supplies in that range: the 12 to 20 V DC input, the 6.0 to 8.4 V pack and the 12 V encoder supply (F4, F9, IOBoard.md summary). The rule-5 reason is not shown either. Digi-Key 0 (18:14:28Z response) only removes the second-vendor route. TCAN1043ADRQ1 (SLLSFD1F Table 4-1) has the same SOIC-14 pin functions: TXD 1, GND 2, VCC 3, RXD 4, VIO 5, EN 6, INH 7, nFAULT/NERR 8, WAKE 9, VSUP/VBAT 10, NC 11, CANL 12, CANH 13, nSTB/NSTB 14. Both enter Normal mode with EN high. Whether it qualifies as the rule-5 alternate is not checked here. JLCPCB C540122: 196, presale 196, DSO-14, as stated.
